script:
const jf = game.folders.find(f => f.type === "JournalEntry" && f.name === "Suggestions"); const folder = await Folder.create({ name: "Ardenford — Misfit Spots", type: "JournalEntry", color: "#b0603a" }); const P = (h) => ({ format: 1, content: h }); const intro = `

Four places three misfits wander into, and the stupid thing they do when they get there. Written for a party that is chaotic neutral with a conscience — not heroes, not villains, and capable of being decent when it is cheap enough.

Each spot gives you the same five things: why they end up there, the dumb ideas they will have, what actually goes wrong, who is standing there when it does, and the heart — one moment where being decent costs them something small and real. That last one is the whole point. Skip it and they are just petty criminals; land it and they are your party.

Encounter budget

Three level-2 characters, 2024 DMG: Low 300 XP · Moderate 450 · High 600. Every "if it goes loud" below is costed against that. XP is from the owned Monster Manual: Commoner 10 · Guard / Bandit / Cultist / Warrior Infantry / Noble 25 · Swarm of Rats / Goblin Warrior / Priest Acolyte 50 · Scout / Tough 100 · Spy / Pirate 200 · Bandit Captain / Berserker / Cultist Fanatic 450 · Guard Captain 1,100.

Guards are AC 16. At level 2 that is a real wall — the watch is not a speed bump, it is a reason to run. Guard Captain at 1,100 XP is nearly twice the High budget: he is not an encounter, he is a losing condition.

`; const market = `

Middle Tier · the Western Market square, hours after the grain and produce stalls shut. 168 walls, 14 lights, ambient night sound.

Why misfits end up here

Because it is the one place in Ardenford that is rich and unattended at the same time. The Western Market runs sunrise to sunset; after dark it is canvas, trestles, locked crates and nobody. The watch walks it, but the watch walks through it, on a rhythm you can learn in one night of sitting on a roof.

Three dumb ideas they will have

  1. Crack a crate to see what is in it. Not to steal — to know. This is the most in-character thing a misfit does and it is how every one of these nights starts.
  2. Take the stall, not the goods. Someone will suggest stealing an entire market stall and setting it up somewhere else. Let them. It is very funny and it is very traceable.
  3. Sell something back to its owner in the morning. Genuinely a plan they will be proud of.

What actually goes wrong

The crate is Greystone grain — federal reserve stock, moved at night on purpose, stamped on purpose. Breaking one open is not theft from a merchant, it is interference with the city's siege stores, and Ardenford has a long memory about granaries. Nobody is chasing them for the value. Somebody is chasing them because of what the stamp means.

Who is here

A night porter who is not supposed to be, counting crates against a list that does not match. He is more frightened of being seen than they are. He will bargain instantly.

If it goes loud

The watch turn-out: 4 × Guard (100) + 1 × Scout as the sergeant (100) = 200 XP — under Low, because this is meant to be survivable and humiliating rather than lethal. AC 16 will still make them work for it.
If they stay and fight the second wave: add 4 more Guards (100) → 300 XP, Low. A third wave brings the Guard Captain, and that is the city telling them to leave.

The heart

The porter has a daughter's name on the back of his tally board. If they let him go — or better, let him keep the discrepancy and take the blame for the broken crate themselves — they have made their first real friend in Ardenford, in the Middle Tier, at night, where friends are useful. It costs them the loot and a night in a cell. That is the price, and they should feel it.

`; const baths = `

Upper Tier · members-only, run quietly by the Vintara Consortium. 188 walls, 23 lights, 25 ambient sounds. Warm, dim, and full of people with their clothes off and their guard down.

Why misfits end up here

Because the Council of Consuls rotates its meetings between keeps so no one keep gains significance — which means the actual conversations happen between meetings, somewhere comfortable, with no minutes taken. Everyone in Ardenford knows this. Nobody says it.

Three dumb ideas they will have

  1. Steal the robes and walk in. It works. That is the problem — it works immediately and then they are inside with no plan and no clothes.
  2. Rob the changing room. An unattended room of rich people's belongings. They will not be able to help themselves.
  3. Get in the water and act natural. The single funniest failure state available, because eventually somebody addresses them by a name that is not theirs and expects an answer.

What actually goes wrong

They overhear something true. Not a grand conspiracy — something small, specific and survivable only if you are already important: a consul's aide arranging for a writ to be posted with no name on it. The party now knows a thing that is worth money to exactly one person and worth their lives to another, and they are naked in a bath house on the Upper Tier.

Who is here

The aide, and a bath attendant who has heard this conversation four times and has learned to be extremely interested in the floor. The attendant is the real asset. She notices everything and is paid to notice nothing.

If it goes loud

Discreet removal: 1 × Spy (200) + 2 × Guard (50) = 250 XP, under Low — but the Spy's job is not to kill them, it is to find out who sent them. Capture is the win condition, and a captured misfit is a much better story than a dead one.
If they kill the aide: Vintara answers. Bandit Captain-equivalent as a Consortium officer (450) + 2 × Tough (200) = 650 XP, above High. That is deliberate. They should lose.

The heart

The attendant will be blamed. She was in the room; they were not supposed to be. If the party walks away clean they will hear, three days later and secondhand, that a bath attendant was dismissed and cannot get work on the Upper Tier. Bringing her with them costs them the clean exit and gains them somebody who knows every face in Ardenford's ruling class.

`; const tap = `

Beneath everything · a tavern in the ancient tunnel network, which the Council insists is sealed. 592 walls, 17 lights, 52 ambient sounds — it is the loudest, wettest, most alive map in the set.

Why misfits end up here

Because it should not exist. Every tunnel entrance inside the city is guarded or sealed, the Council is emphatic about it, and there is a bar down there with a full room. Finding it is a status symbol. Being known down there is a career.

Three dumb ideas they will have

  1. Win a drinking contest against a dwarf. Yes. Yes they will.
  2. Run a tab. Nobody down here uses coin for everything, and the alternative currency is favours. They will find this out after the third round.
  3. Ask loudly how everyone gets in and out. The one question that gets a room to stop talking.

What actually goes wrong

Nothing, at first — and that is the trap. They are welcomed, fed, and on the way out somebody hands them a sealed package and a name, in a tone that makes it clear this is the tab being settled, not a request. Refusing is allowed. Refusing means they were down here, they saw it, and they owe nothing — which makes them a loose end rather than an asset.

Who is here

Working dwarves who move goods under the city because the surface routes are taxed and watched. They are not villains and should not read as villains: this is an economy, not a cult. Khargrom-dur (Ardenford — Townsfolk) fits perfectly as the one who vouches for them — a valley guide is exactly the sort who knows the ways under as well as the ways east.

If it goes loud

The room turns: 6 × Bandit as off-shift smugglers (150) + 2 × Tough (200) = 350 XP, just over Low — in a flooded, pillared, 592-wall space where line of sight is terrible and everyone but the party knows the floor plan.
Do not let them win by killing. The tunnels are a place they need to be able to come back to. Give the room a reason to break it up.

The heart

One of the smugglers is moving medicine, not contraband — Willowglass stock, cheaper under the city than over it, going to Gray District families who cannot pay Upper Tier prices. If the party burns the tunnel to the watch for a reward, that supply stops. Nobody will ever tell them that happened. That is the version of consequence that works on a party with hearts: not punishment, just a thing quietly getting worse somewhere they cannot see.

`; const library = `

Upper Tier, Ridge District · built into and around an intact ancient structure. 456 walls, 13 ambient sounds, no placed lighting — see the note below.

Why misfits end up here

Because the Ruins Reclamation Act made ruin-delving legal and profitable, and the Concordance holds the maps and the old expedition reports. Every treasure hunter in Ardenford comes through here. The party will come here for a map and leave with a problem.

Three dumb ideas they will have

  1. Just take the book. The entire plan. There is no second step.
  2. Tear the page out so the book stays on the shelf and nobody notices. Somehow worse.
  3. Get one of them to distract the Magister. This will involve a false accent and it will not survive contact.

What actually goes wrong

They are not caught by the Magister. They are caught by Elarion Faenwynd, the elf archivist, who does not raise an alarm — he asks what they are looking for. And he can read what they cannot. Whatever they wanted is genuinely in his hands now, and he has decided to be curious about them instead of turning them in. They have accidentally acquired a patron, and they will not notice for several sessions.

Who is here

Magister Ellyn Merrick — stern, protective, believes knowledge should be shared provided you handle it with respect. She is not an obstacle to beat; she is an obstacle to impress, and she can be impressed.
Elarion Faenwynd — archivist and translator, guest scholar from Araethilion. Both are already built in Ardenford — Townsfolk.
Pell Orvaine at The Still Page, one lane over, knows every Concordance staffer's tea order and is a soft way in for a party that thinks to try being nice.

If it goes loud

It should not. The Concordance is the spot in this set that punishes violence with irrelevance — fight here and the doors close to them permanently, which costs more than any fight. If you must: 2 × Priest Acolyte (100) + 4 × Guard (100) = 200 XP, and the real consequence is being barred, not beaten.

The heart

Elarion is far from home and nobody in this city can pronounce his name. If a player asks how to say it properly — eh-LAR-ee-on FAYN-wind — and gets it right, he will help them with things he is not supposed to help them with, for years. It costs nothing but attention. Misfits who are bad at everything except noticing people are the best kind.

⚠ Map note

This scene ships with zero lights. If you run it with token vision on, the party is in the dark in a library. Either set the scene's global illumination on, or lean into it and run it after closing.

`; const je = await JournalEntry.create({ name: "Ardenford — Misfit Spots", folder: folder.id, pages: [ { name: "How to run these", type: "text", text: P(intro) }, { name: "1 · Western Market, after dark", type: "text", text: P(market) }, { name: "2 · The Vintara Baths", type: "text", text: P(baths) }, { name: "3 · The Drowned Tap", type: "text", text: P(tap) }, { name: "4 · The Concordance Library", type: "text", text: P(library) }, ], }); return { journal: je.name, folder: folder.name, pages: je.pages.map(p => p.name) };

Correct the inaccurate map note about library lighting and add an accurate note about the night market's darkness level

Create the six named misfit-spot NPCs with correct ring tiers and dress the Ardenford Watch guard actor

script:
const je = game.journal.getName("Ardenford — Misfit Spots"); const add = async (pageName, html) => { const p = je.pages.getName(pageName); await p.update({ "text.content": p.text.content + html }); return p.name; }; const market = `

On the board — 7

The situation: a buy is happening at the fountain at the worst possible hour, and the one honest witness is forty feet away with his own reason to say nothing.

  • Sella Redcott (green — talkable) · at the fountain. Buying something off a seller who has already left. She is not dangerous herself; the two at the braziers are hers and she will spend them without blinking. Lever: she pays under value and knows it. A party that has something to sell has an instant in.
  • Redcott's Man ×2 (grey — muscle) · under the two lit braziers, west and east. Deliberately placed on the plaza's two lit approaches, so the party is already between them before anyone speaks. Not a wall — a pair of eyes that will follow.
  • Wick Harlow (green) · south-west crate stack. Counting federal Greystone crates against a tally that does not match, because he has been skimming one sack in forty for eleven months. His daughter's name is inked on the back of the board. Lever: he will bargain instantly, and he will not fight.
  • Three nobodies (ringless) · a sweeper closing a west stall, a young woman cutting through the south stalls, an old man on the stoop of the lit house. They are there to make it a place rather than a set, and to make "nobody saw us" a lie.

To pick a fight: walk between the braziers. To be in the way: the sweeper is closing the exact stall they want. As a lever: Harlow's tally board — it is evidence against a consul's supplier and against Harlow, and he knows it.

`; const baths = `

On the board — 7

The situation: the aide thinks the baths are safe because they always have been. Everyone else in the building is either naked, working, or paid to stand still.

  • Aldric Dunwick (green) · the middle private soaking room, east side. Mid-conversation about a writ posted with no name on it. Isolated by design — the party can reach him, but only past the minder.
  • Vintara Minder ×2 (grey) · the corridor outside the private rooms, and the head of the entrance stair. One covers the prize, one covers the way they came in. Neither is looking at the canal dock in the south-west — that is the way in the map is quietly offering.
  • Nessa Brightmoor (green) · the attendant's desk, west. Has heard this conversation four times. Knows every face in Ardenford's ruling class by the state of their feet. Lever: the single best-informed person in the building and the only one nobody is watching.
  • Three nobodies · two in the main pool, one in the banquet room. Unarmed, unclothed, and extremely willing to scream.

To pick a fight: the corridor minder, in a tiled room, with no armour on anyone. To be in the way: the bathers between the pool and the private rooms. As a lever: Nessa — and remember she is the one dismissed for it if strangers are found, which is the page's heart.

`; const tap = `

On the board — 8

The situation: nothing is wrong. The room is warm, the welcome is real, and the tab is running whether they asked for one or not.

  • Brogmar-dur (green) · behind the counter. Keeps the place. Runs no coin tab — the currency is favours and he decides what one is worth. Lever: genuinely hospitable, which is exactly how the debt gets made.
  • Khargrom-dur (green) · the round table. Already a townsfolk actor. He is the one who vouches for them, which is why the room relaxes — and why they owe him before they owe anyone else.
  • Tunnel Runner ×2 (grey) · shifting barrels on the walkway below the tap, and on the east walkway. Working, not watching. One of them is moving Willowglass medicine, not contraband — see the heart, above.
  • Tap Lookout (grey) · head of the stair down. The only one whose job is the party. Placed so leaving is a decision, not a default.
  • Three nobodies · a drinker at the second table, someone at the kitchen hearth, a boy running messages on the lower walkway. The boy is the fastest way for news of the party to reach anywhere in the undercity.

To pick a fight: ask loudly how everyone gets in and out. To be in the way: the Lookout on the stair. As a lever: the tab — and the boy, who can carry a message anywhere down here for the price of being nice to him once.

`; const library = `

On the board — 6

The situation: quiet, sparse, and the most dangerous room in the set — because losing here costs them access, not hit points.

  • Magister Ellyn Merrick (green) · the long reading hall. Stern, protective, believes knowledge should be shared provided you handle it with respect. Not an obstacle to beat — an obstacle to impress, and she can be impressed.
  • Elarion Faenwynd (green) · the north shelves, cataloguing. Positioned exactly where a thief would reach for a book. He is the one who catches them, and he does not raise the alarm — he asks what they are looking for.
  • Corr Ashgate (grey) · the east apse, watching. A ruin-delver with a forged Reclamation writ, after the same report. Happy to let the party take the risk and then take the map off them outside. The only one here who will start something — and he will do it in the street, not in the building.
  • Ardenford Watch (grey) · the south stair. One guard, AC 16, CR 1/8. He is not a fight, he is a witness, and that is worse.
  • Two nobodies · an apprentice copying at the south bench, someone crossing the lower chamber.

To pick a fight: don't — take it outside with Ashgate, who wants exactly that. To be in the way: the apprentice is at the desk they need. As a lever: Elarion, if a player bothers to learn to say his name.

`; return { updated: [ await add("1 · Western Market, after dark", market), await add("2 · The Vintara Baths", baths), await add("3 · The Drowned Tap", tap), await add("4 · The Concordance Library", library), ], tokenCounts: game.scenes.filter(s => s.folder?.name === "Ardenford — Misfit Spots") .map(s => `${s.navName}: ${s.tokens.size}`), };

script:
const card = ({ line, type, was, now, voice, wants, lever, tell }) => `

${line}

Type: ${type}

Was: ${was}

Nine bodies against three PCs looks scary, but the 4 conscripts (9 HP) die to any AoE and the priestess has 38 HP. Without Fireball (no focus yet) the party leans on Synaptic Static (Caven, V/S) and Burning Hands/Scorching Ray (Marrith), so budget 3 slots. With Fireball back it is 2 slots. The Sergeant\'s AC 18 and the two Veterans\' Parry are what make it take 3 rounds, not the mooks.', tac:'The apprentice opens with Darkness (reskinned innate) over the party while the Veterans fire heavy crossbows (poison-coated: on a hit, DC 13 CON save or poisoned for 1 minute) from behind the conscripts. The priestess casts Bless on the Sergeant and Veterans, then Spirit Guardians, and walks into Caven (AC 12). The Sergeant uses the conscripts as a screen and multiattacks whoever is Wild Shaped. Conscripts flee at half numbers; the apprentice Misty Steps to a rooftop and casts Faerie Fire on whoever is hiding in the dark. They want capture, not kills: the first PC to drop gets netted, which is the GM\'s cue to slow-roll lethality.', ter:'A stalactite-street switchback with web-bridges 20 ft overhead (DC 12 Athletics to climb; the webs are flammable and conduct Fireball nicely later). Bystanders: slaves and goblin hawkers who scatter; collateral is a House Barrabin propaganda win and raises the bounty. Hook: the Sergeant carries the bounty writ naming all three PCs with sketched faces, listing their confiscated gear as "held by the Quiet Debt" (the Bounty Hunter). This is how the party learns where their gear is.', sc:['Down: drop the Priest (3,050) or the Apprentice (3,050).','Up: add a second Sergeant (4,600), or swap the Apprentice for a Scout Captain on the web-bridge (3,750).','Replace the 4 conscripts with 2 Knights for a hard Low (4,800).']}, {n:'The Quiet Debt (Bounty Hunter)',xp:'5,900',d:'Low (solo)',role:'Main path, fight 3 (after the short rest): the gear hand-back moment.', cost:'About 4 slots (Hold Monster/Blight attempts against good saves, Shield reactions, one Healing Word), 20-25% party HP, 1 Wild Shape. HP 137 and AC 19 with Cunning Action and Smoke Bomb mean spell attacks miss and he vanishes between turns; this is a chase fight, not a damage race. Cheaper in slots than its XP suggests because there is only one target to control: Talo\'s Wild Shape grapple or Caven\'s Hold Monster (once the pouch is back) ends it. Danger: he single-targets Caven (AC 12, 86 HP) with poisoned blades for 30-40 a round; if Caven has no Shield yet he can lose half his HP in one round.', tac:'He has trailed them since the Patrol fight. He opens from a rooftop in Darkness with a hand crossbow (drow poison: DC 13 CON or poisoned; on a failure by 5 or more, unconscious for 1 hour, which is the capture tool), then drops Smoke Bomb and closes on the softest PC. Cunning Action to disengage every round; he never ends a turn adjacent to Talo\'s bear form. At half HP he retreats upward along the webs (spider-silk gloves, climb speed) and taunts: he will sell their gear back for a price, or trade it for one of the three. If the party uses Greater Invisibility or Pass without Trace he loses them, and the GM can pivot this to a non-fight.', ter:'A market square with a 30-ft stalagmite column and web-lines to three towers; levitation discs (reskinned innate Levitate, once per day) let him break line of sight. Hook: he carries a satchel of confiscated gear, which is where the GM can return Marrith\'s arcane focus and/or Caven\'s component pouch. The rings and Talo\'s staff can be elsewhere (Rival House, Procession). A side pouch holds a Barrabin bounty writ and a second writ from House Ilphrin offering more, seeding the Rival House pivot.', sc:['Down: swap for the Assassin (CR 8, 3,900) as "a House Blade": same tactics, 97 HP, hits harder but folds faster.','Up: add 2 Death Dogs (CR 1, 200 each) as his trackers (6,300, still Low; move him into a subfolder "Bounty Hunter\'s Pack" if you do).','Moderate: the Street Patrol\'s survivors arrive on round 3 (a second Sergeant + 2 Veterans = +2,500, total 8,400).']}, {n:'Sorcere Response Squad',xp:'8,400',d:'Moderate (set-piece)',role:'Main path, fight 4: the layer\'s exit at the cavern gate. Run only with gear restored and after the short rest.', cost:'The expensive one: 6-8 slots (a Counterspell duel with the Mage burns 2-3 L3+, Wall of Force or Hold Monster on the Weapons-Master, one Fireball/Cone of Cold, 2 Healing Words or a Heal), 35-50% party HP, 1-2 Wild Shapes, Stone\'s Endurance x2. 274 total enemy HP; Mage AC 15, Commander AC 18 and HP 161. The Mage\'s Fireball (28 average) on three clumped PCs is the single biggest damage swing in the layer. Caven\'s Counterspell is the answer, and the Mage has Counterspell back, so expect 2 counterspell exchanges. Designed as Moderate: could go badly without healing.', tac:'A textbook drow kill-box. Scouts on the gate towers open with Faerie Fire (reskin) on the party so the Mage has no disadvantage. The Weapons-Master uses Tactical Charge into Caven on turn 1 and Counterattack against anyone who swings; he fights to hold the gate, not to chase. Scouts keep shooting whoever is lowest. If the Mage drops below 30 HP he Misty Steps through the gate and flees; the Weapons-Master surrenders only if the Mage is dead and he is below 40 HP (a drow does not die for a lost gate).', ter:'The city\'s lower gate: a 20-ft-wide arch under a portcullis with two 25-ft towers; the exit tunnel beyond is a natural chokepoint. Hook: the Weapons-Master wears Talo\'s staff lashed to his back as a trophy, or the gatehouse strongbox holds the remaining gear. Killing the Mage here means the Caves layer has one fewer pursuer.', sc:['Down (to Low, 5,000): replace the Weapons-Master with a Guard Captain + 2 Knights (1,100 + 1,400). Same gate fight, far less HP to chew through.','Down further: Mage + 2 Knights + 4 Scouts = 4,100.','Up: add a Scout Captain on the second tower (9,100).','Never add a second caster: two Counterspelling Mages against a party with about 6 L3 slots left is Deadly by attrition.']}, {n:'Procession of the Spider Queen',sub:'Priestess Procession',xp:'5,150',d:'Low',role:'Alternate: substitute for main-path fight 2, or avoided entirely with Pass without Trace. The priestess (HP 127, AC 16, Fireball for 28 to all three, Scorching Ray, Hellish Rebuke) is the one real threat. The acolytes\' Hold Person on Marrith or Caven is the swing: two paralyzed PCs make this Moderate in practice. The mooks are Fireball fodder, there for spectacle, not math.', tac:'Zesstra does not start hostile: a procession stops traffic in a plaza, celebrants chanting, the quasit invisible and scouting the crowd (it spots the PCs and whispers). If fought: celebrants form a body-wall around her, acolytes cast Hold Person then Spiritual Weapon, she casts Fireball from behind the wall and Hellish Rebukes anyone who hits her; she retreats toward the chapel at half HP. If parleyed: she is Barrabin\'s rival within the temple hierarchy and will take a bribe (the 300 gp diamond, Talo\'s gilded flower, i.e. material components the party wants back) to look the other way, or will escort them past the Patrol in exchange for a future favor to Lolth (Caven\'s necromancy interests her).', ter:'A fungal-lit plaza with a 10-ft raised dais and a spider idol; the crowd of about 40 bystanders gives three-quarters cover and is a reason not to Fireball. Hook: the procession is heading to the chapel where a yochlol is in residence (see Handmaiden of Lolth); attacking the procession triggers that off-path set-piece. The quasit is the party\'s chance to notice they are noticed: Perception 16 spots it.', sc:['Down: drop one acolyte (4,700) or the quasit (4,950).','Up: add a Priest (reskin "Zesstra\'s second") for 5,600.','Full Moderate reveal: the Yochlol steps out of a celebrant\'s skin, 5,150 + 5,900 = 11,050, just under the 11,100 Moderate ceiling. Only if the party has a short rest banked and gear back.']}, {n:'Rival House Retinue',xp:'7,350',d:'Moderate (if fought)',role:'Off-path pivot (house politics): a buyer, an ally of convenience, or a Moderate fight if they insult him.', cost:'If fought: 5-6 slots (Tsabrak has Shield and Fly, so spell attacks miss and he kites; Hold Monster or Wall of Force to pin him, Fireball for the knights), 25-35% party HP. His Shatter and Befuddlement target saves the casters are good at; the Knights (AC 18, Parry) screen him and hurt Caven in melee. As a parley it costs nothing but a future obligation.', tac:'He finds them; they do not find him. The hangers-on hail them from a levitating palanquin. His offer: Ilphrin smuggles them out of the city (bypassing the Response Squad at the gate) in exchange for killing or humiliating a Barrabin target (the Weapons-Master, or burning the Barrabin chapel). If refused rudely he "collects the bounty himself": Fly up, Befuddlement on Caven, Shatter on the group, knights charge; hangers-on run. He yields the moment he is Held or below 50 HP; a prodigy does not die in the street.', ter:'A noble terrace 40 ft above the street with a stair and two web-ramps; fighting here is in the open with no bystanders (the hangers-on are the bystanders). Hook: he holds the second bounty writ (seeded on the Bounty Hunter) and knows where Barrabin stored one piece of gear, the clean way to deliver Caven\'s rings. A deal converts the Sorcere Response Squad into a "they walk through the gate under Ilphrin colors" scene, or re-routes them to the Web-Lane Ambush as the smuggling route.', sc:['Down to Low: drop the two Knights (5,950).','Up: add a Mage Apprentice house tutor (7,800).','If they take his deal and double-cross him, he returns in the Caves with the Knights as a Low fight.']}, {n:'Market Cutthroats',xp:'3,950',d:'Low',role:'Alternate: a cheap fight 2, and the "they lose gear again" threat. Without Fireball it costs about 4 slots because the mooks die in twos. Jhaelryna\'s Hold Person and Blinding Flash are the only real threats; her illusions waste a round or two.', tac:'Twelve bodies are the point: the ambush teaches the party they outclass the street. Cutthroats swarm from stalls with nets and hand crossbows (poisoned, DC 13 CON) to drop a PC and strip gear. The Spies use Cunning Action to pickpocket (Sleight of Hand against passive Perception) any recovered component pouch. Jhaelryna casts Blinding Flash, then Hold Person on the healer, and vanishes in Minor Illusion smoke to let the gang work. The gang breaks at half numbers; the Boss surrenders and sells information (the Bounty Hunter\'s lair, the gate schedule).', ter:'The lower bazaar: narrow web-roofed lanes, stalls as half cover, a slave pen that can be opened as a distraction, glowfungus stacks that burn. If the Spies lift a pouch, chasing them down is a mini-pursuit, not a fight.', sc:['Down: drop Jhaelryna and run Boss + Spies + 8 Bandits (1,050) as a nuisance.','Up: add a second Bandit Captain (4,400) or 4 more Bandits (4,050; more Fireball fodder, still Low).']}, {n:'Web-Lane Ambush',xp:'4,100',d:'Low',role:'Alternate fight 2, and the smuggling route out of the city (links to the Caves).', cost:'3-4 slots (Fireball on the webs is the obvious play; Hold Monster or Moonbeam on the Drider; one Healing Word), 15-25% party HP, poison saves. The Drider (HP 123, AC 19) is a wall: spell attacks miss, so this is a save-or-suck fight. The Phase Spiders\' Ethereal Jaunt plus poison bites on Caven are the damage; they pop in, bite and pop out, wasting PC actions. Web-restrained PCs lose turns; Talo\'s bear form shrugs webs off.', tac:'A pure Lolth ambush. The Drider casts Darkness on the lane\'s exit and Faerie Fire on the party, then Web to restrain the lowest-Dex PC. Giant Spiders shoot webs from above; Phase Spiders jaunt in to bite restrained targets and jaunt out. The Drider only enters melee against a restrained PC and flees up the web wall at 40 HP. It is not Barrabin\'s: it is an exiled Barrabin daughter cursed by Lolth, and it hates the house more than it wants the party. A DC 18 Persuasion or an offer to burn a Barrabin target turns it into a guide to the Caves (and a recurring face there).', ter:'A web-lane: a 60-ft vertical shaft threaded with thick web-bridges between tower-stalactites, difficult terrain for anyone without spider climb, and flammable (a Fireball burns a 20-ft section, dropping anyone on it 20-40 ft). No bystanders; the city does not go here. Hook: the far end exits the city wall: the smuggler\'s route Lord Ilphrin offers, and the bypass around the Sorcere Response Squad.', sc:['Down: remove the Phase Spiders (2,700); the Drider plus two web-spiders is nearly free.','Up: add 2 more Giant Spiders (4,500) or a third Phase Spider (4,800).','Do not add a second Drider: two AC 19 walls is a slog, not a threat.']}, {n:'House Gate Guardian',xp:'2,900',d:'Low (solo)',role:'Off-path: if they try the Barrabin compound or treasury to recover gear. A puzzle-fight.', cost:'2-3 slots if solved, about 10% HP. The Shield Guardian (HP 142, AC 17, Regeneration, a stored spell) is a damage sponge; brute-forcing it costs more slots than it should. The honest cost is time and one or two L4-L5 slots, which is why it is a guardian, not a fight.', tac:'It stands in the Barrabin treasury antechamber and does nothing until the door is forced; then it attacks whoever carries the enemy mark (the bounty writ). The stored spell is Hold Person (a House priestess loaded it), cast on the first PC through the door. It does not pursue beyond the compound. The controlling amulet hangs on the Weapons-Master (Sorcere Response Squad) or in the treasury itself; stealing it turns the guardian into an ally for one scene (a 142-HP meat shield for a party with no martial is a real prize).', ter:'The treasury: a 30 by 30 ft stone room, two doors, a stored-spell glyph. Hook: this is where the GM can put the bulk of the recovered gear if the party goes looking for it instead of chasing the Bounty Hunter. The amulet is also a Rival House bargaining chip.', sc:['Up: add 2 Gargoyles (reskinned House statues, 450 each) on the facade for 3,800 (move to a subfolder "Treasury Wardens" if so).','Down: let the stored spell be Shield instead of Hold Person.']}, {n:'Handmaiden of Lolth',xp:'5,900',d:'Low by XP, plays Moderate',role:'Off-path set-piece: only if they attack the Procession or enter the chapel. Magic Resistance makes every DC 17 save-or-suck a coin flip in its favor; HP 153; Caustic Lash hits hard; and Dominate Person on a party with no martial means a dominated Marrith Scorching-Rays her friends. Toxic Escape lets it leave at will, so the GM controls the length. Pure damage is the honest path, which drains slots.', tac:'It wears a celebrant\'s shape in the Procession, or a priestess\'s in the chapel, and reveals itself only when the party has committed to a fight or desecrated the idol: Web the exit, Dominate Person on the squishiest caster (Caven, AC 12) and turn him on his friends, then Caustic Lash whoever tries to break the domination. It wants one of the three as a trophy for Lolth, not a massacre; at half HP it goes gaseous through the ceiling vents and the party is marked. It can reappear in the Caves.', ter:'The chapel of Lolth: a 40-ft web-vaulted nave, idol dais, ceiling vents (its exit), four celebrant alcoves. Hook: the reliquary holds a component the party wants (the gilded flower, the Revivify diamond). Killing a handmaiden here makes Barrabin\'s priestesses permanently hostile in the Caves.', sc:['Down: it leaves at 100 HP instead of 76 (it is not committed).','Up: stack it onto the Procession as the Moderate reveal (11,050). The mooks die to the first Fireball and the fight is really Priestess + Yochlol, a heavy, honest Moderate.']}, ]; const pages=[]; pages.push({name:'Overview',type:'text',sort:0,text:{format:1,content:`

Drow Streets: the hunt in the streets

The escapees are loose in the city of House Barrabin, the house whose prison they just broke. Three pressures run at once:

  1. Barrabin's official response: patrols, a mage-led response squad, a bounty posted on the escapees.
  2. The city as predator: cutthroats who smell soft surface-walkers with no gear, a drider in the web-lanes between stalactite towers, a Lolthite procession that stops traffic.
  3. House politics as the pivot lever: rival House Ilphrin wants to buy the escapees before Barrabin recovers them, and a priestess can be bribed or played off a rival.

Gear

The party enters with Talo's healing intact (V/S) but Marrith and Caven still lacking foci. Fights before the Bounty Hunter are shaped for V/S-only casting (Scorching Ray, Burning Hands, Synaptic Static, Blight, Eyebite, Conjure Animals, Wild Shape). The Bounty Hunter carries confiscated gear as proof of the bounty and is the natural hand-back for a focus/pouch; fights after him assume Fireball, Cone of Cold and Wall of Force are back online. Other gear hooks: rings with Lord Ilphrin, Talo's staff on the Weapons-Master or in the gatehouse, components in the chapel reliquary, bulk gear in the Barrabin treasury.

Recommended main path (4 fights, one short rest)

#EncounterXP / DifficultyExpected costCumulative
1Street Patrol3,500 Low~3 slots, 10-15% HP, 0-1 Wild Shape3 slots, ~15% HP
2By route: Market Cutthroats (3,950, bazaar), Web-Lane Ambush (4,100, up and over), or Procession of the Spider Queen (5,150, plaza, parley-able)Low~3-4 slots, 15-25% HP6-7 slots, ~35% HP, 1 Wild Shape
SHORT REST (a web-loft, an Ilphrin terrace, or the Drider's lair): Marrith regains sorcery points (Sorcerous Restoration), Caven recovers 6 slot-levels (Arcane Recovery, e.g. 2x L3), Talo regains 1 Wild Shape, Hit Dice bring the party back near full.
3The Quiet Debt (Bounty Hunter), solo5,900 Low~4 slots, 20-25% HP, 1 Wild Shape. Gear hand-back.4 slots, ~25% HP (post-rest)
4Sorcere Response Squad (gate)8,400 Moderate~6-8 slots, 35-50% HP, 1-2 Wild Shapes, 1-2 Stone's Endurance10-12 slots post-rest; party at ~40-60% HP entering the Caves with Talo's Heal and most L4+ slots untouched

Layer total: roughly 16-19 of the party's 57 spell slots and 2-3 of Talo's Wild Shapes (plus one Wild Resurgence swap). Comfortably within "win without running dry", provided no fight is escalated to Moderate before the rest.

Pivots

  • Rival House Retinue (Moderate, 7,350) can replace fight 4 entirely (they walk through the gate under Ilphrin colors) or convert the Response Squad to its Low version (5,000).
  • House Gate Guardian (Low solo, 2,900) is the alternate gear-recovery route if they go into the compound instead of after the Bounty Hunter.
  • Handmaiden of Lolth (Low solo that plays Moderate, 5,900) is the consequence of attacking the Procession. Never run it in the same rest window as the Response Squad.
  • If the party avoids fights with Pass without Trace or Greater Invisibility, let it work. The Bounty Hunter and the gate squad are the two to keep as "they find you anyway".

Budget reminder (DMG 2024, three level-12 PCs)

Per character at level 12: Low 2,200 / Moderate 3,700 / High 4,700. Party of three: Low 6,600, Moderate 11,100, High 14,100. Aim mostly Low and Moderate, an occasional High only as a set-piece, never Deadly by design. The question is not whether they win, but whether they win with spells, HP and healing left for the next fight.

Drow reskin (all humanoid stat blocks)

No drow stat block exists in the 2024 books, so every humanoid is a reskinned Monster Manual NPC. Add at the table: Fey Ancestry (advantage vs. Charmed, magic can't put it to sleep), Sunlight Sensitivity (irrelevant underground), Darkvision 120 ft, at-will Dancing Lights, 1/day each Faerie Fire and Darkness. Driders, spiders, the quasit, the yochlol and the shield guardian need no reskin.

Actor folders

Encounters > Drow Streets. Solo actors (Bounty Hunter, Shield Guardian, Yochlol) sit at the folder root; each group encounter has its own subfolder. One actor per stat block; drop the count shown in each table. Each actor carries flags.pentaryn.encounter {name, count, tier, xpEach}. Nothing is placed on a scene.

`}}); E.forEach((e,i)=>{ const mine=acts.filter(a=>a.flags.pentaryn.encounter.name===e.n); const rows=mine.map(a=>{const f=a.flags.pentaryn.encounter;return `@UUID[${a.uuid}]{${a.name}}${f.source}${f.count}${crs(a.system.details.cr)}${f.xpEach.toLocaleString('en-US')}${f.tier}${a.system.attributes.hp.max} / ${a.system.attributes.ac.value}`}).join(''); const content=`

Drow Prison: the break-out

Environment. The cell-block, kennels, interrogation wing, chapel and gate of a drow House's private gaol (House Barrabin). Pitch dark throughout: no PC has darkvision and Light is a material-component cantrip, so Talo's Produce Flame and Fire Bolt are the party's only light. Narrow corridors and barred doors, webbed ceilings where watch-spiders roost, a drain/cistern level beneath, an oubliette pit, a small Lolth chapel, and a gate yard where the alarm converges.

Theme. Jailers and slave-beasts, a House interrogator who holds the party's confiscated gear as "evidence", spiders bred as watch-beasts, a priestess overseeing the gaol, and other inmates who can be freed as allies or stirred into a riot. The party is under-equipped (no foci, pouches or magic items: V/S spells only, Wild Shape intact), so every fight here is Low and rewards cleverness over raw damage.

Budget reminder (DMG 2024, party of 3 at level 12)

LowModerateHigh
6,60011,10014,100

Design goal: no single fight drains them. The question is "can they win and still have spells, HP and healing for the next one". Layer = 3-4 fights, at most one short rest. Main path total 12,550 XP across four Low fights, deliberately light because the party has no gear.

Recommended sequence

  1. Cell Block Turnkeys (2,700) — about 3-4 L1-L2 slots, Wild Shape 1, 15-25% HP.
  2. Interrogation Chamber (3,200) — the gear drop. 2 L3 (Counterspell duel), 1 L4-L5, 1-2 L1, maybe Wild Shape 2, 25-35% HP if the Fireball lands.
    Cumulative after two fights: roughly 7-9 slots spent (2-3 L3, 1-2 L4+), Wild Shape 1-2 used, party around 50-65% HP, Talo down 1-2 Healing Words.
  3. SHORT REST in the drain cistern reached from the chamber's side door (or in the Lightless Cells if they hide). Caven Arcane Recovery (6 slot-levels, e.g. two L3), Marrith Sorcerous Restoration, Talo regains a Wild Shape use, hit dice bring them to about 85-90%.
  4. Spider Kennels (2,900, upper route) or Drain Pudding (1,100, lower route, skips the kennels, arrives behind the Warden) — 1-2 L3 (Conjure Animals), 2 L1-L2, Wild Shape 1, about 20% HP.
  5. Warden's Gate (3,750) or Riot in the Yard (2,650, if inmates were freed, with Ryld pulled in) — 1 L5, 1 L3, 1 L4, 3-4 L1-L2, 2 Healing Words, 25-35% HP.

Expected state leaving for the Streets: each caster has roughly 1 L6, 1 L5, 1-2 L4, 1 L3 and a couple of L1-L2 left; Talo 0-1 Wild Shape with Wild Resurgence available; party HP 55-70% with Heal (L6) in reserve. The Interrogation Chamber gear is back in hand, so Streets fights can assume Fireball, Web, Wall of Force and Goodberry.

Off-path pivots

  • The Oubliette (3,350) — if they drop the pit or want the hidden postern.
  • The Handmaiden (5,900, plays Moderate) — the one fight that can leave them short: the price for poking the chapel, never a required gate.
  • Lightless Cells (1,400) — a quick ambush or a hiding-place complication.

If the players take two pivots on top of the main path, cut the Spider Kennels/Drain fight or let the Riot replace the Warden's Gate so the layer stays at four fights.

Foundry layout

Actors: Encounters / Drow Prison. Solo encounters (Drain Pudding, The Handmaiden) sit directly in the folder; group encounters have their own subfolder. One actor per stat line; drop the listed count of tokens. Each actor carries flags.pentaryn.encounter (name, count, tier, xpEach). Nothing is placed on a scene.

Theme: The Hunt and the Gate

Open Underdark between the Barrabin city and the surface: webbed galleries, a lightning-scarred chasm, echoing hook-horror warrens, a fungal hollow, and a drow watchpost at the sunward exit. The party is mostly re-equipped by now (foci recovered; Fireball, Cone of Cold, Wall of Force and Summon spells online), so budgets run at true level-12 strength.

The drow do not garrison the caves; they HUNT them. Two drow pressures bracket the layer: a pursuing elite squad closing from behind (the House wants its prisoners back quietly) and a fixed watchpost at the only sunward exit (the standing watch, which has been warned). Between them the caves are indifferent and lethal. Drow options use darkness, poison, webs, faerie fire, levitation and ambush; the non-drow options let the GM pivot the instant the party leaves the marked path.

Budget reminder

Three level-12 PCs: Low 6,600 / Moderate 11,700 / High 14,100 XP. Goal is not "can they win" but "can they win and still have spells, HP and healing for the next one". Every fight before the finale stays under the Low ceiling; the finale is the only High. Never Deadly-by-design. Party pool: roughly 57 spell slots and ~283 HP; at most one short rest in this layer.

Recommended main path (4 fights, one short rest)

#EncounterXP / difficultyExpected costRunning total after
1Web Crossing2,800 Low~3-4 low slots (one L3, two L1), 15-25% HP on one PC~4 slots, ~15% party HP, 0-1 Wild Shape
2House Hunting Squad6,400 Low (caster duel)2 L3 Counterspells, 1 L5, 1-2 Shield, 2 Healing Word, maybe 1 Wild Shape; 35-45% HP before heals~11-12 slots incl. 1 L5 and 3-4 L3; party HP ~55-60%; 1-2 Wild Shapes
SHORT REST (squad dead or retreated to report). Caven Arcane Recovery (6 slot-levels), Marrith Sorcerous Restoration (SP back, convert to slots), Talo 1 Wild Shape back and Wild Resurgence, 3-4 Hit Dice each (~25-30 HP per PC). Re-enter at ~85-90% HP with ~48 slots, 2-3 of them L5+. Spore Hollow is the ideal rest site; otherwise the drow supply cache beyond Echo Gallery.
3Echo Gallery OR Vhalyss the Unmade2,800 Low / 2,300 LowEcho: 3 slots L3+ (maybe two L5 walls), 20-30% HP. Vhalyss: ~3 slots incl. one L4+, 10-20% HP~15-16 slots spent of 57; 1-2 L5+ left per caster; HP 65-75%; Talo 1-2 Wild Shapes
4Sunward Gate Watchpost12,600 High (set-piece)Most remaining L4-6 slots, 1-2 Counterspells, Heal once, 2 Healing Words, all SP and Wild ShapeSunlight 200 ft past the arch is a hard escape line. One PC likely under 25% HP; nobody is required to fall.

Finale readiness check: they should arrive with at least 8 L3+ slots between them, Talo's Heal (L6) unspent, and one wall spell left. If not, run the gate at 11,200 (remove 2 Wardens) or down to Moderate.

Pivots by direction

  • Party goes UP a chimney: The Thing on the Ceiling (3,900 Low; yields the gate watchword).
  • Party crosses the chasm: Lightning in the Chasm (7,200 Moderate). If taken, skip Echo Gallery and route to the gate; it eats two L5+ slots.
  • Party goes DOWN into worked stone: Duergar Toll-Gang (3,650 Low, or a parley that can remove Wardens/Trackers from later fights, or sell a back door past the gate).
  • Party follows glowing fungus: Spore Hollow (1,950; the breather and best short-rest site).
  • Party doubles back: drop Vhalyss onto the Hunting Squad's position.

Total layer XP if everything were fought: 43,500. Main path alone: 24,600 (Low, Low, Low, High).

Gear recovery points

  • Web Crossing: dead drow scout, hand crossbow + 6 poisoned bolts.
  • Hunting Squad: War-Mage carries one confiscated party item (focus or ring).
  • Echo Gallery: supply cache, 2 healing potions, spare leathers.
  • Lightning in the Chasm: caravan wreck, component pouch + Druidic focus.
  • Spore Hollow: hand crossbows, 12 poisoned bolts, gate roster.
  • Sunward Gate: gatehouse strongroom holds the rest of their gear.

Actors > Encounters > Underdark Caves. Solo encounters sit directly in the folder (Vhalyss the Unmade, The Thing on the Ceiling, The Chasm Behir). Group encounters have subfolders: Web Crossing, Hunting Squad, Echo Gallery, Sunward Gate, Duergar Toll-Gang, Spore Hollow. One actor per type; drop the listed counts.  ["Lone Peak", { ...common, category: "place", parent: null, skill: "his", dc: 10, whenKnown: "advantage",

purpose: Write Caven's Ramblings into his player-only story journal
script:
const html = "

No sun, no moon, no stars. I could've been here for years. Does my body even age? My hair, it grows. My heart pumps blood, but what does that even mean? Since my death — since my death, I have found nothing to explain how I am still connected here. I move my fingers one at a time and it's like pulling the strings of a puppet. That's not my hand, it's the hand of one of my risen undead — but no, it is me. Do I see through my eyes, or is it my eyes that see through my eyes? That doesn't make sense, yet it is.

…

My father's book had a when. Who went in, when, what came back up. That's the whole point of the thing — without the when it's just a list of names. I've got no when. No sun, no dawn walk, nothing. I'm keeping a ledger with one name in it, and the date column is fucking empty.

…

The drow archives had little on what I needed to advance our understanding. They know how to make the corpse move, but they don't fundamentally understand how they are reanimating the body. Might as well worship the gods to make the body move for them — useless wizards, might as well call themselves clerics. Yet here I am, with the same level of understanding of how I am writing this journal, how I move this limb across the page, how my hand is somehow able to write clean cursive while my instructions to write are so distinct. What if I'm not me? Could I be split? What if I'm trapped in a body being controlled by me? — No, that does not make sense. If I was not me, then I wouldn't see myself as me — wait.

Okay, maybe I can communicate with myself. I will stop willing the movements and just observe.

[The pen slips down slightly, and a small blot of ink builds up in one spot.]

— Nothing. There's nothing there. So it's just a vessel.

…

Clean cursive. Of course it's clean — it's his. My father's. I learned my letters off the book of the drowned, tracing his hand. Same slope on every page. So when I stop willing it and the pen still wants to go, that's not me, and it's not nothing either — it's — that's him in the hand. — No. Habit. Habit is nothing. Same as the blot.

…

I have discovered more about my condition in this cell, for who knows how long, than I did in the weeks sneaking around in the drow archives. Not exactly reaching enlightenment here.

…

If I die here, will my soul be trapped wherever it is? Maybe I'm going in the wrong direction. Instead of trying to be whole again, I should destroy this body and be done with it. What if I'm not tethered here, though? I'm a summoner. I've summoned myself, so I'm not tethered — I'm stuck. My soul is stuck, so there's no tether to break but the one I made. Did I make it because I was stuck, or did I make it while in transit? Transit meaning my soul was on its way somewhere.

…

Destroy this body — ha. That's my father's job. Stake it, burn it, write it in the book. He never once asked where the thing he was burning had gone. To him there was nobody in there; it was just the fen being the fen. I say the same thing — nobody home. He puts them in the fire and I put them to work, and only one of us is the monster. Fuck that. I asked. Look where asking got me.

…

Is necromancy inherently evil if it was used to help people? I did good in this world, but in the eyes of the gods, does doing that good through necromancy make it inherently evil? Why not hell? Maybe doing good with evil netted me this plane of existence. I did good, dammit. I saved lives. The bodies are bodies; they have no use anymore, they are not helping anyone. I took what was dead and made it helpful. There are no souls in bodies. Once someone's dead, their soul has moved on. They don't need it anymore.

…

I am bound to this body MY body — my body — what if I unbind, like I do when I raise a corpse? But I can't. I close my eyes and I don't feel a self. There's no me. I'm — wait — a wisp in the planes. If there's no me, how am I looking through my eyes? If there's no me, then how did I cast the spell? Did I do it with thought? I'm no sorc. I need my spells, my hands, components. I'm no witch; there's no sort of mystic power behind my magic. So, maybe — maybe if I can find a way to unbind myself, I can see where I'm at. Even the color of the plane my soul — or mind — or whatever — if I knew the color, I could have a starting point.

…

Fuck monks. Meditation and gaining a higher sense of awareness. I am in some higher plane, and all the meditation in the world has yielded no results in learning what higher plane I am at. Monks spend their whole life gaining higher power, higher understanding. Here I am, in some higher plane — it's not all it's cracked up to be. What are they proving by not using tools? They think they're above it all.

…

Sometimes the shard glows just bright enough that I can see the monk in the other cell. God, he hasn't moved an inch for... I don't know, we'll say 100 glow cycles. That's the average time it takes for my shard to get to its peak brightness. And I just see his silhouette.

…

Just that shape, dead still. My father stood like that. Edge of the causeway, first grey light, not moving, just looking at the flats to see what came up overnight. I'd be behind him with the book, freezing my ass off, and he wouldn't move for an hour. I never asked what he was looking for. Maybe stone still is how you see.

…

1000 glow cycles. ± 1000, depending on if I dozed off. The monk is still there, like a stone, not moving. Fuck him. He's probably dancing around my wisp self in the higher planes. I have yelled at him many times, ordered him to tell me his secrets. Not even a flinch. I'm nothing to him, aren't I? Well, fuck him.

…

5000 glow cycles, ± I don't know, 10,000. The guard today threw another prisoner into the cell. There was never a monk; I'm just seeing shapes in the stone. Ha — stone still. He was literally stone still. Fuck my life.

Wonder if they forgot I was in here. When was the last time I ate? Did I run out? How long ago was it? — I do not need to eat. Good to know.

Okay, I still retain my spells. I should start considering how to use them, over trying to learn how to meditate. Clearly I'm no monk.

"; const j = game.journal.get('jr9nCVYh4cq0DTpS'); await j.update({name: "Caven's Ramblings"}); await j.pages.get('1rQJRoswfNVLwVic').update({name: "Caven's Ramblings", "text.content": html}); const p = j.pages.get('1rQJRoswfNVLwVic'); return {name: j.name, page: p.name, len: p.text.content.length, ownership: j.ownership, hasQuintus: /quintus|emperor|empire|throne/i.test(p.text.content)};

script:
const p = game.journal.get('YT9kVkZAHmEcyUnX').pages.get('RYd4Qeda7m7FtNB2'); if (!p.text.content.startsWith('

You walked down off Ulearos')) return {aborted:'journal changed since read', start:p.text.content.slice(0,120)}; await p.update({'text.content': "

They took my pack and my staff. They left me my clothes, and under the silk at my wrist they left the one thing I would have fought them for, because they did not know to look. No chains. To them I am a local whose papers have lapsed, and I will sit in this stone room until someone decides what I am.

I am good at waiting. I learned it the way I learned most things worth knowing: by doing it wrong first, for years.

…

I was born on a piece of the sky that fell. Where I come from, that is not a way of speaking. Outsiders call it Lone Peak, one mountain standing where no mountain has any business standing. We call it Ulearos. It is an old word. No one can tell you what it means anymore, and we keep it anyway.

The mountain was a city once, and the city flew. When it fell it drove itself into the land like a thrown spear. It scraped the sky on the way down, and what came off with it was us. Every Groundstruck has a star up there that is truly theirs, and a life is the time it takes to learn which one. When we die we burn, so nothing holds us, and we go up to know the sky once again.

We are not afraid of dying. What we fear is dying before you have found your star, when the sky has no place made for you yet, and you may go nowhere at all.

…

My brother's name was Oriaro. Nobody called him that except our mother, when he was in trouble, which was often. He was Ori. He was younger than me by enough years that I had carried him on my shoulders.

The city was built for wings. The first shape a star druid learns is a winged one, because that is how you cross the street, and no one teaches it. You watch, and then you jump.

So he watched me. A whole season, at my elbow on the east ledge, while I went out and came back, out and came back. Every time I landed he would roll his eyes and say let me be among the stars again, Talo, which is what we say when we are sick of someone. Between brothers it was a joke, the mildest use there is. I cannot hear it now without my jaw going tight.

I made him watch anyway. By the end of the season I could see it in how he stood at the edge. Loose, not braced. You cannot shift braced. His shape was a little grey bird, the quick kind that nests in the cliff cracks, and it was holding longer every day.

The night before, we sat on the lip with our legs over nothing, and Ori asked me if he was ready. I told him the truth. You're ready. Tomorrow, I'll be there.

He grinned at me like I had handed him the whole sky.

…

The next morning a climber came over the lip of the summit.

There is no way up Ulearos but wings or a long, honest climb, and anyone who makes it is fed and housed. I saw him first, so I walked him in. I sat him by a fire and put bread in him, and he asked about the sky, and I liked being listened to. That is all it was. I was looking the other way, at a stranger's face.

Ori got tired of waiting. A boy waits about as long as he can stand to and then not one breath longer. He meant to jump, come round the shoulder of the mountain on his own wings, land beside me and watch my face. I know, because it is what I would have done.

The east wind is moody in the mornings. Once in a long while it drops away for a breath and comes back from somewhere else. He jumped into that breath, and the grey came halfway into his arms and went out of them, and there was nothing under him to buy a second try.

I did not see it. I have decided, many times, that I saw it anyway. That is one of the things I am still learning to set down.

There was a feather on the ledge afterward. Small, grey, from the shape he had almost finished becoming. It has been under the wrap on my wrist every day since. I have never told anyone it is there.

…

We burned him that night. Then the druids sat the trial, because he had died before he found his star.

There are two questions. Did he likely know his star? He did not; he was too young. And how tied was he to the world? That one took a long time, because people kept coming forward to say how he was loved, and by whom, and it was most of the mountain. The druids said a soul tied that tight does not fall through. He would be born again. No fault. An accident. The wind.

No one blamed me. I want to be exact about that, because I spent years being inexact. Not the druids. Not my mother, who held my face in her two hands to say it. Not my father. Even the climber, before he left, found me and said he was sorry, as if it had been his.

You would think it would help. If one person had said you promised him, I would have had something to push against. Instead everyone was kind, and you cannot push against kind. You only sink. I turned my own words over until they wore smooth. Tomorrow, I'll be there. I had told him the truth, and then I had been somewhere else, enjoying being listened to, and everyone was so careful with me I could not breathe.

…

Here is our law. Kill a Groundstruck before they find their star, and you are locked away from the sky, underground, for years. No Groundstruck chooses the deep. No one on the mountain would send me there.

So I sent myself.

I would not take wings down. I would not let the sky carry me away from the sky. I climbed down Ulearos hand over hand, the way the stranger had come up, with my family on the ledges above me calling for me to stop, and I did not look up. That was the true sentence, the one no druid could have handed me. I went into the deep, and I stopped looking for my star.

It was easier to be guilty than to be forgiven. Guilt was something I could do.

…

I will not count the years. There were many.

On Ulearos the wind never stops. Down here nothing moves unless something moves it, and at first I thought the stillness would take my mind. I thought that was the point. It did not. Fungus grows on nothing, in places no one has ever stood, and does not feel sorry for itself. I hauled for a mushroom farmer in the wet caverns for a long stretch and slept on sacks, and I learned more about patience from a mushroom bed than I ever learned sitting still on purpose.

The drow took me in the way a city takes in a stray. No one ever mistook me for one of them. I was the big grey thing at the bottom of the ladder. But after enough years I was theirs. Once a child threw a stone at me in the street, and a woman cuffed him for wasting a stone on someone who lived there. In its way, that was a home.

I still wake every morning at the hour Ori jumped. There is no morning down here, and I wake anyway.

And the sky would not let go of me.

A star druid's power comes from the night. Underground it dims, and I had told the sky I was finished with it. I expected it to go out. It never did. It sat in my chest like a coal under ash. Some nights, with all that rock over me, it would stir, and the flecks on my arms would show faint through the dust, and I would have to sit down. For years I was angry at it.

Slowly I understood what it was doing. Not forgiving me; I did not want that. Waiting, the way he had waited on the ledge.

…

The deep taught me this last, and it took all those years. The law says years. It does not say forever. Somewhere in there I stopped paying a debt and started hiding, and it took me a long while to tell the difference.

And there was the other half, which took me longest. When I went down the mountain, my mother and father did not lose one son. They lost two. One to the wind and one to the ground, and only one of those was an accident. I owe them a son back. That debt I can pay.

The guilt is not gone. I do not think it goes, and I think it would be wrong if it did. But there is a difference between carrying a thing and being flattened by it, and I found that difference down here, where I had come looking for nothing. I am carrying it now. I am bringing it home.

The healing is not finished. I have come as far as stone can bring me. The rest has to happen on Ulearos, in the wind, in front of my family, whatever is in their faces. Once I could not have said that. I need to stand on the east ledge and say his name out loud, the whole of it, Oriaro, into the wind. I have not said it aloud since I left. After that, I think, I can look up and start looking for my star again.

…

The trouble is the way up.

I know the deep better than I know my own mountain now. The way out I let go of on purpose, long ago, because I thought I was never leaving. The drow watch the roads to the surface the way we watch the sky: always, and on principle. I went up through tunnels I did not know, got lost for the first time in years, and walked straight into a patrol.

They looked me over and did not draw. Not an enemy. A local in the wrong place, and no one yet sure which place I belong in.

So I sit on stone, which I know, with my wrist in my other hand over the place where the feather is. My hands are still. When they come to ask what I am, I will tell them: a goliath of the Groundstruck, going home, late.

Tomorrow, I told him once. I'll be there.

I am late. I am coming.

"}); return {len:p.text.content.length, start:p.text.content.slice(0,80)};

script:
const MM="Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor."; const crownDesc=`

Wondrous Item, Artifact (Requires Attunement)

A narrow circlet of black iron, scabbed with rust and hollow along its whole length, so it weighs almost nothing. Put to the ear, it murmurs. Whoever wears it hears whispers: many voices, never quite in step, speaking as if from the far side of a wall.

The Whispers. While you wear the Crown, you hear the whispers constantly. They know things they shouldn't, and they lie when it suits them.

Hollow Majesty. While attuned to the Crown, your Charisma score increases by 2, to a maximum of 24.

Listening Through Walls. While attuned to the Crown, you can cast Detect Thoughts (save DC 15) from it. After you cast the spell, roll 1d6. On a roll of 1–5, you can't cast it again in this way until the next dawn.

Doubt. While attuned to the Crown, you have Disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

The Errand. The first time you attune to the Crown, the whispers give you a quest of the DM's choosing. You can't use Hollow Majesty or Listening Through Walls until you complete it.

Curse. The Crown is cursed. Once you attune to it, you can't remove it or end your Attunement to it voluntarily, and Remove Curse has no effect on it. Completing the Errand, or the Crown's destruction, ends the curse.
